metadata.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array

problem_summary.summary: Return the first and last indices of a target in a non-decreasing array, or [-1, -1] if it is absent.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a sorted integer array nums, which may be empty, and target. Return a two-element array containing the inclusive range of target indices or [-1, -1].
constraints: The required algorithm runs in O(log n) time

brute_force.explanation: Scan the array once, recording the first and most recent index equal to target. If no match was recorded, return [-1, -1].
brute_force.correctness_idea: The first matching position encountered is the left endpoint, and each later match updates the right endpoint. Since the array is sorted, all occurrences are contiguous; after the scan the recorded endpoints cover them all.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space, excluding the two-element returned array.

optimized.explanation: Run binary search twice: once for the first index with value >= target, and once for the first index with value > target. If the first bound is at the end or does not equal target, return [-1, -1]; otherwise the range is [first, upperBound - 1].
optimized.correctness_idea: The lower bound marks the earliest possible occurrence and the upper bound marks the first position after every occurrence. Their difference spans exactly the contiguous target run; checking the lower-bound value handles absence.
optimized.time_complexity: O(log n): two binary searches, each over n elements.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space, excluding the two-element returned array.

steps.event: Start lower-bound search for the first value >= 2.
steps.condition: 2 is not less than target, so the lower bound is at mid or earlier.
1 < 2, so index 0 cannot be the lower bound.
steps.action: Set left to mid + 1; the bound is index 1.

steps.event: Start upper-bound search for the first value > 2.
steps.condition: For an upper bound, a value equal to target must be skipped.
8 > 2, so the upper bound is at mid or earlier.
5 > 2, so the upper bound is at mid or earlier.
steps.action: Set right to mid; the bound is index 4.

edge_cases.handling: The lower bound is 0 == nums.length, so the result is [-1, -1].
The lower-bound value differs from target, so the result is [-1, -1].
The bounds are 0 and nums.length, yielding the full range.
The two bounds differ by one, so both result endpoints are that index.
